introduction: Delaware unemployment insurance offers temporary payments to qualifying workers. Initial claims and weekly benefit requests are separate steps.
description: Delaware unemployment insurance offers temporary payments to qualifying workers. Initial claims and weekly benefit requests are separate steps.

sections.who: The agency reviews recent wages, why work ended and whether you remain able, available and seeking work. A monetary determination alone does not establish every eligibility condition.
sections.get: Weekly payments depend on an approved claim and continuing eligibility. Report earnings and other required payments accurately.
sections.docs:
• Employer and wage history.
  • Job-separation information.
  • Pay stubs or other wage evidence, especially if reported wages seem incomplete.
sections.apply:
1. File the initial or reopened claim

    Use the claim link at Delaware DOL Unemployment Insurance.

  2. Review the wage determination

    Check that employers and wages are correct; ask the agency how to challenge an error.

  3. Request benefits each week

    Use the current weekly filing instructions, including WebBenefits or TeleBenefits options, and keep work-search records.
sections.after: Read every notice and retain confirmations. Continue weekly claims while a dispute is pending, as instructed by the agency.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Delaware UI claims and contacts; Claimant responsibilities and FAQs. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Does the initial application request every future week?
No. Weekly benefit requests are separate.
Contact the agency promptly and supply wage records.
Can I claim while an appeal is pending?
The state directs claimants to continue weekly filing.
